identity: Highcourt is safe inside its walls; outside them, private collectors dress their charges as royal tolls.

quests.title: A Hearing for the Absent
quests.text: A report from Goldmead names a woman, Pella Thatch, entered among the cargo under a capital toll mark. Alis Cartwright of The Charter of Stone can check the transport pledges with the army's supply office. Speak to her at the Miner's Guild house here in Highcourt; I want Pella's account heard before another claim travels under our city's mark.
quests.completion: I want to know who needs that load and who is driving it; a neat total tells me neither. I'll take up Pella's case with the supply office and check what was actually agreed. People do not become part of a shipment because someone finds room for them on the page.

variants.text: Word from Copperfell puts a counting-house stamp on stolen purses used to pay a goblin foreman's crew. Take the report to Hadrin Beamset of The Charter of Stone at the Miner's Guild house here in Dur Brannoc. He works with the army's supply office and knows what our marks should cover. I would like a better answer than 'it had a stamp on it'.
variants.completion: I'll ask the supply office which crew is short, what work has stopped and whether everyone came back. Tovin Ashthumb's name stays with this report. A tally that accounts for every lump of ore and loses the carter needs doing again.

variants.text: A report from Starbough says the bough-seal is being used to claim timber and labour that were never granted. Speak to Caelir Veinward of The Charter of Stone at the Miner's Guild house here in Lethariel. She works with the army's suppliers and knows the limits of each release. We should establish what the mark permits before anyone makes the forest pay for a generous reading.
variants.completion: I will take up the report and compare the releases with our suppliers' records. Every permission has a purpose and an edge; we ought to be able to show both. Nima Fern's account deserves more than a glance at a seal.

quests.lesson: Chapter 1 opens at the envoy at 19 with no prerequisite; a walk to the capital's Miner's Guild house.

quests.title: What a Seal Allows
quests.text: The army's supply office and I have stopped a load here in Highcourt: its sealed record claims the drivers can be reassigned along with the goods. Their agreement was to deliver a load, and I want the record checked before anything moves. Secure the dispatch record in the yard beside the butcher's shop and bring your findings back to me.
quests.completion: The seal covers a delivery agreement and nothing more; I reject the added order over the drivers, and the supply office has sealed that finding with me. The load goes to its proper recipient, with the drivers' agreed work unchanged. We still do not know how those papers reached the people misusing them; a report of withheld supports in Frostbarrow Shelf gives us another place to look.

variants.text: The supply office and I have held a load of material for tools at Dur Brannoc's ore yard. Its record claims the crew has been transferred, which would mark their supply as settled while they work with worn tools. Secure the dispatch record on the ore yard's loading apron and bring your findings back to me. A clean stamp will not hold a failing tool together.
variants.completion: The original order names the crew that needs this material; I reject the claimed transfer, and the supply office has sealed that finding with me. The material goes to those miners as intended. We still have to learn how outsiders obtained these papers, and the withheld supports reported in Frostbarrow Shelf need the same close look.

variants.text: Our suppliers and I have paused a release of material for tending and repairs here in Lethariel. Its covering sheet claims much more timber, and the tenders' labour along with it. Secure the dispatch record at the timber check beside the bowyer's workshop, then return to me. I want to see where a limited permission became an open claim.
variants.completion: The original release covers tending and repairs; the wider claim on timber and labour does not stand, and our suppliers have sealed that finding with me. They will issue the material for its agreed purpose. How these papers reached outside hands remains unanswered; the dispute over supports in Frostbarrow Shelf may help us follow their path.

quests.lesson: A spot in the capital town (a town place) and back; the leader decides the capital's case, the papers' source stays open.

quests.title: Light for the City's Work
quests.text: Petitioners still wait outside the chapel after dark, and a person carrying a complaint should at least be able to see the steps. Bring me twenty Torches for the queue and the paths leading here. I have enough reports of injustice without adding a badly lit stair.

variants.text: Petitioners still wait outside the chapel after dark, and a person carrying a complaint should at least be able to see the steps. Bring me twenty Torches for the queue and the paths leading here. I have enough reports of injustice without adding a badly lit stair.

Late carts arrive while the gate watch is changing, usually just as someone puts out the useful light. Bring me twenty Torches for the watch and the approaches to the ancestor hall. The ancestors can wait patiently; a driver with a wheel in a rut seldom does.

The tenders use the paths beneath the old trees long after the light has left them. Bring me twenty Torches for their rounds. We will keep the flames low and clear of the boughs; the trees have entrusted us with enough already.

A recruit ought to leave the muster yard watching the road, instead of feeling for it with a boot. Bring me twenty Torches for the yard and the marching routes. I want the first lesson of the evening to involve something better than falling over.

The pilgrims' boardwalks to the cenote need light after dark. Bring me twenty Torches so a thoughtful walk does not end with a startled splash. People come here to speak to the water; most would prefer to do it standing above it.

The living come to visit the graves after their day's work, and they still need light to find the right names. Bring me twenty Torches for the paths. We have time to wait for them; there is no need to make their walk harder.

quests.lesson: A Basic craft at the first capital visit: coal and sticks, no profession.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS. Draft §4 and K12 A: every envoy asks for Torches for the capital's own services; one title, the occasion in each capital's voice.

quests.title: Debts That Walk at Night
quests.text: Debtbound Zombies wander the {name:commons} after dark, reaching for travellers as though another toll were due. Lay two to rest and report to me. No account I keep entitles a collector to do that.

variants.text: Debtbound Zombies wander the {name:commons} after dark, reaching for travellers as though another toll were due. Lay two to rest and report to me. No account I keep entitles a collector to do that.

Debtbound Zombies come through the {name:pastures} at night to collect debts that were settled long ago. Lay two to rest and bring me word. I keep the receipts, but they have shown very little interest in reading them.

Debtbound Zombies trample the young growth in the {name:glades} after dark and turn on anyone tending it. Lay two to rest and return to me. The tenders need a safe path, and those dead have walked it long enough.

Debtbound Zombies walk the {name:blightfields} at night, grasping at people over debts that stand in none of our records. Lay two to rest and bring me word. An empty claim should not keep making victims.

quests.lesson: A short night hunt on the capital's outskirts; a third of a day hunt's count.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS. Draft §4 and K12 A: one shared night task against the Debtbound Zombies in four capitals; the night count about a third of the day hunts' (ruling 12).

quests.title: A Steady Hand for a Rash Promise
quests.text: I told the guards that a calm record-keeper could shoot as well as any of them, and they have thoughtfully arranged a chance to demonstrate it. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I before my mouth makes any more promises on my hands' behalf. Highcourt's Alchemy trainer at the herb garden in the lore quarter teaches the recipe. Sunleaf and a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars can be found back where you started; travel from the city's waystone to your first village's waystone for a quick return.
quests.completion: Thank you; that should steady my hand, if not the judgement that made the claim. I have left room on the score sheet for an honest result.

variants.text: I mean to win a throwing match against an old pan plate, while Varda has made me promise the good pan will survive. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I to help my aim catch up with my confidence. Dur Brannoc's Alchemy trainer at the brewhouse on the terraces teaches the recipe. For Sunleaf and a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars, take the city's waystone to your first village's waystone; it is a quick trip back where you started.
variants.completion: Good, now the old plate has reason to worry. The useful pan is staying in Varda's kitchen, where it can witness none of this.

variants.text: Someone remarked that envoys only ever hit upon decisions, and I have agreed to answer with a bow. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I; I should like the reply to land where I intend. Lethariel's Alchemy trainer at the brewhouse among the homes teaches the recipe. Sunleaf and a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars are found back where you started, a quick journey from the city's waystone to your first village's waystone.
variants.completion: Thank you; I still have to draw the bow and aim it. Should I miss, I expect the next remark to be considerably better prepared.

variants.text: I told a recruit that the target was the large round thing in front of him, and now he wants to watch my turn. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I before the rest of the yard gathers. Gor Drazhak's Alchemy trainer at the herb house in the bone quarter teaches the recipe. Take the city's waystone to your first village's waystone for a quick trip back where you started; you can find Sunleaf there and get a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars.
variants.completion: Right, my turn. If I miss, the recruit has earned one comment, and I suspect he already knows which one.

variants.text: I promised to shoot a fruit hanging on a cord before Teshani calls it back to the kitchen. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I; supper is approaching faster than my confidence. Kezamba's Alchemy trainer at the herbalist's under the vines teaches the recipe. For Sunleaf and a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars, travel from the city's waystone to your first village's waystone for a quick return to where you started.
variants.completion: Thank you; I will take my shot before Teshani takes her fruit. She says a miss counts as returning it undamaged.

variants.text: My score on the old shooting list has stayed unremarkable for nearly a century, so I rashly announced that this year's attempt would be worth recording. Bring me an Elixir of Precision I for the attempt. Nhal Veyr's Alchemy trainer at the physic house in the market teaches the recipe. Sunleaf and a Boar Tusk from the daytime boars can be found back where you started; the journey from the city's waystone to your first village's waystone is reassuringly quick.
variants.completion: I will record the score exactly as it falls. If it is worse, at least the list will finally contain something new.

quests.lesson: Learn Alchemy at the capital's trainer, gather where you started, brew at the capital's Brewing Stand; a friend's elixir counts too.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS. Plan §2 point 6, §2a points 4-5, draft §4 'Die Alchemy-Aufgabe' and K13 A: one shared quest, one elixir everywhere (Precision I: Sunleaf, Boar Tusk, Glass Bottle), each envoy's own playful occasion; the text names the trainer's plot in words and sends the player back where they started by their start settlement's waystone, never naming the start zone. The one quest the r45_st check lets ask for a grug_alchemy item.

quests.title: The Last Unauthorised Stamp
quests.text: Bandit Tollmaster Penn presents his private collections as royal tolls, complete with a stamp intended to end the conversation. Kill him at the {name:toll_camp}, {dir_from_giver:toll_camp}, and report to me. I have heard enough complaints from people who paid because they thought our city had ordered it.
quests.completion: Penn's collections end here. I will put his misuse of the royal mark on record so the people he threatened can have their complaints heard.
quests.lesson: The capital's named leader at his camp, alone: the capital's local finale.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: a new id (its objectives changed); free play, a level only.

quests.title: A Peg for the Bread Board
quests.text: My bread board rocks, and the royal kitchen offers replacement pegs on terms longer than the board. Bring me one Gnarled Boar Tusk; Furrow Boars in the {name:commons} can provide one by day. I can fit it myself without obtaining permission to cut a loaf.
quests.lesson: A daytime errand that leaves your enchant stock alone.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the id stays (objectives unchanged); free play, a level only.

quests.title: The Long Table
quests.text: The palace has ordered venison for the long table and left the hunting arrangements with the man standing beside an oven. Hunt six Fallow Bucks by day in the {name:commons}. I will see to the meal; it seems somebody ought to see to the deer.
quests.lesson: Neutral daytime game on the capital commons.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the id stays (objectives unchanged); free play, a level only.

quests.title: The Empty River Baskets
quests.text: I paid for river baskets and received a very confident promise, which has proved difficult to bake. Ask Merren Oakstamp at Whitebridge Market Close what became of the order. She knows the trade, and I would like to hear her account of it.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the handover id stays; free play, it requires nothing and claims no earlier deed (draft §10).

quests.title: Bread for the March
quests.text: The watch at Cinderline stands between our homes and the fighting, and they are fond of receiving their bread before it goes hard. Go and offer Toren Waterbarrel help at Cinderline Watch in Ashenward March. Whatever else he needs, I expect it matters just as much to the people waiting for it.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the handover id stays; free play, it requires nothing and claims no earlier deed (draft §10).
